name: Insider Collusion
summary: A person with legitimate access supplies information or suppresses a control so that an external party can take cargo. The insider rarely handles the goods. What they provide is far more valuable: knowledge of which load is worth taking, when it moves, and which check will not be performed.
how_it_works: An individual with legitimate access identifies high-value consignments and their timing.
That information, or an access credential, is passed to an external party.
A control that would normally detect the loss is bypassed, delayed or performed without scrutiny.
Cargo is taken through what appears operationally to be a normal process.
The absence of forced entry and the correctness of the paperwork direct the initial investigation away from the origin site.

indicators.signal: Losses concentrate on consignments whose value was known internally but not externally visible from packaging or documentation
indicators.observable_in: Comparison of loss set against externally observable value cues
indicators.notes: The strongest structural indicator. If the targeting could not have been done from outside, it was informed from inside.

indicators.signal: Events cluster on a specific shift, gate, workstation or supervisory approval rather than distributing across the operation
indicators.observable_in: Loss events aggregated by shift, location and approver

indicators.signal: The control that would have caught the loss was, in each case, the one not performed or performed by the same individual
indicators.observable_in: Control execution log against loss events

indicators.signal: Access, override or exception authority used outside the pattern normal for that role
Losses stop abruptly during an unannounced audit or a staffing change and resume afterwards
indicators.observable_in: Loss timeline against audit and roster changes
indicators.notes: Close to conclusive when it recurs, and it is the reason unannounced controls are worth more than scheduled ones.

indicators.signal: Undisclosed relationship between an employee with award or approval authority and a counterparty
indicators.observable_in: Conflict-of-interest declaration compared against register data

false_positives.looks_like: Losses concentrated on one shift or individual.
false_positives.actually: That shift or person simply handles more volume, or handles the higher-value flow by design.
false_positives.how_to_rule_out: Normalise by exposure. Compare loss per consignment handled, and test whether volume alone explains the concentration before treating the person as the explanation.

false_positives.looks_like: A control was not performed on the affected movements.
false_positives.actually: Systemic under-resourcing, in which the control is skipped routinely across the operation under time pressure.
false_positives.how_to_rule_out: Measure the control's execution rate overall. If it is skipped at a similar rate on unaffected movements, the finding is a process failure and not evidence of collusion.

false_positives.looks_like: An employee has a connection to a counterparty.
false_positives.actually: An entirely innocent connection in an industry where local employment and supplier networks overlap heavily.
false_positives.how_to_rule_out: Establish whether the individual actually influenced the award or the control, since a disclosed and non-influential relationship is a governance matter, not a fraud finding.

preventive: Separate the person who knows a consignment's value from the person who executes the release, so that neither role alone is sufficient.
Restrict visibility of consignment value on a need-to-know basis rather than exposing it throughout the operation.
Require conflict-of-interest declarations from anyone with award, approval or override authority, and reconcile them against register data rather than accepting them at face value.
Rotate assignments and approvers on high-value flows and use mandatory leave to create natural control gaps.
detective: Aggregate loss events by shift, gate, workstation and approving individual, normalised by volume handled.
Monitor override and exception authority for use outside role-normal patterns.
Run unannounced controls and compare loss rates during and outside them.
Maintain a confidential reporting channel and treat reports as an evidential lead rather than a personnel complaint.
responsive: Preserve access logs, CCTV and rosters before initiating any interview, since these are the records most likely to be lost once the investigation becomes known.
Normalise by exposure before drawing any conclusion about an individual, because this pattern has the highest personal cost of a wrong call in the entire taxonomy.
Involve HR and legal from the outset so that evidence remains usable and the process remains defensible.
Close the information asymmetry that made targeting possible, since replacing the individual without changing the access does not close the exposure.

regulatory_hooks.relevance: A documented risk analysis of direct suppliers must identify this pattern class where the carrier population plausibly exposes the company to it.
A functioning complaints procedure is both a legal obligation and, in practice, one of the most productive detection channels for this pattern.

regulatory_hooks.provision: Protection of persons who report breaches
regulatory_hooks.relevance: Insider-facilitated loss is frequently first surfaced by a colleague, so whistleblower protection is directly operative.
